neighbours.label: Statements about when something is at its extreme over time (its best / lowest / peak time of year or day); fires on the extreme word or the following temporal preposition, where a time period is expected
fire: The lake is at its clearest at this time of year, before the algae return.
Demand for heating oil hit its peak in January and dropped once the thaw began.
The best time to plant garlic is when the soil has started to cool.
Mosquito numbers are at their highest during the weeks right after the rains.
The market is at its busiest in the hour before the stalls close.
Nights are longest and coldest at this point in the winter, just after the solstice.
The best time to photograph the canyon is when the sun is low.
River levels reached their lowest in late summer and rose again with the autumn storms.
quiet: The lake is behind the old mill, past the row of poplar trees.
Heating oil is delivered by truck and stored in a tank under the porch.
We planted garlic along the fence and covered the bed with straw.
Mosquito nets hung over every bed in the small clinic by the road.
The market sells bread, cheese and olives from stalls under a tin roof.
My uncle keeps his winter coats in a trunk at the foot of the stairs.
The photographer carried two cameras and a tripod into the canyon.
The river runs past the village and under a narrow stone bridge.

notes: Card: ' in', ' during', ' when' after 'minimum', 'darkest', 'best time'. Output (reversed) suppresses ' peak'/' period'. Probes: 'looks its best at this time of year' 0.60, 'reached their peak in December and fell' 0.64, plain location sentence 0.005.
